title: Volume of an Open-Top Box Constructed from a Cardboard Sheet
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: An open-top box is constructed from a rectangular sheet of cardboard measuring 14 in. by 22 in. by cutting out equal squares of side length x in. at each corner and folding up the sides. Express the volume V of the box as a function of x and state its physical domain.

steps.title: Express the Box Dimensions in Terms of x
steps.explanation: Removing a square of side x from both ends of the 14-in. side reduces the base width to 14 - 2x. Removing a square of side x from both ends of the 22-in. side reduces the base length to 22 - 2x. Folding up the flaps creates a box of height x.
steps.why: Each corner cut removes x inches from both ends of each dimension of the rectangle.

steps.title: Determine the Physical Domain Restrictions
steps.explanation: For all three dimensions of the box to be strictly positive, we require x > 0 and 14 - 2x > 0, which restricts x to the open interval (0, 7).
steps.why: The shorter side of length 14 inches limits the corner cut x to strictly less than half of 14, which is 7 inches.

steps.title: Multiply the Dimensions to Obtain Volume V(x)
steps.explanation: The volume of a rectangular box is the product of its height, width, and length: V(x) = x(14 - 2x)(22 - 2x).
steps.why: Volume equals base area (14 - 2x)(22 - 2x) multiplied by altitude x.
